name: Single Leg X Control
keyCorrections: If they free their leg, your lock was too shallow — re-enter with a deeper lock behind their knee.
If they flatten your hip foot, you lost distance control — re-post immediately before they close the space.
If they grab your head, swim your hand inside their arm and pummel back to their collar.
description: Full control of the opponent's single trapped leg with both legs in SLX, enabling sweeps to top position, back takes, or leg lock entries.
shortInstruction: Lock the leg, control the hip, own the base — SLX is control, not survival.
summary: Single-leg X control goes beyond the basics — it means you own the opponent's trapped leg completely. They cannot free it, cannot step out, and cannot base on it. From this level of control, every option is available: you can sweep them to their back, take their back when they post, or drop into a leg entanglement. The difference between basic SLX and SLX control is the depth of your lock and your ability to read and react to their weight shifts.
whyItWorks: A properly locked SLX gives you the mechanical advantage of two legs against one — they cannot simply pull free.
Controlling the hip with your foot prevents them from circling out or stepping around your guard.
Your proximity to their center of mass means every weight shift they make is telegraphed through the trapped leg.
Danaher principle: the transition from SLX to the finish should be continuous — control through motion.
commonMistakes: Locking the SLX too loosely — a loose SLX gives them the freedom to step out or posture.
Focusing only on the trapped leg and forgetting to hand fight — their hands can still attack your head.
Staying in SLX too long without attacking — your legs will fatigue, and they will escape.
Letting them grab your hip foot and remove the post.
coachingCues: Lock tight, hip high, stay active.
Their leg is your steering wheel — feel every move.
If you're comfortable in SLX, you're not attacking enough.
Flow through SLX — don't camp there.
safetySummary: Protect your own knee when they try to spin out of the SLX — release and re-enter if you feel twisting.
Keep your hip foot active to prevent them from grabbing and controlling your ankle.
When sweeping from SLX, control your own fall to avoid landing badly on your back.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Deep SLX lock → hip foot posted → feel weight shift → attack sweep, back take, or leg entanglement.

decisionTree.action: sweep them backward over the posted leg.

moneyDetails: Your SLX lock should be behind their knee, not at the ankle — knee-level lock gives you maximum leverage.
The hip foot should be driving into their hip bone, not just resting — active pressure changes their base.
Maintain a sleeve or wrist grip on their far arm to prevent them from posting or grabbing your head.
When they post a hand to defend the sweep, that arm is now committed — attack the armbar or transition to the back.
nextStep: After mastering SLX control, learn the advanced sweeps and the continuous transition to X-guard.
fixItFast: They keep pulling their leg free? Lock higher — behind the knee, not the calf.
Can't sweep? Your hip foot is too passive — drive it into their hip as you pull the trapped leg.
They grab your foot? Pummel your foot to a different angle — don't let them settle their grip.
